verdict.rationale: Asana's own docs say its in-app AI Teammates have shared memory that carries forward feedback and preferences, so users don't repeat context they've already given. That is a first-party, preference-learning capability, but it is framed as team-level work memory, not personal adaptation to an individual's tone or shorthand. Missing for 10: evidence of learning an individual user's writing tone, evidence of learning personal shorthand, documentation of how preferences shape output style, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have my in-app AI assistant learn my tone, shorthand, and preferences to tailor its output

citations.quote: Shared memory means AI Teammates learn from the work itself. Every completed task, every piece of feedback, every preference gets carried forward, so no one repeats context they've already given
Pre-built AI agents that work alongside your team inside real workflows, with shared memory, governance, and context from the Work Graph
